\mxunit{enrichment-pigeonhole-problems}{The pigeonhole principle}
\mxsubtitle{High school · olympiad thinking \textperiodcentered{} Synthesis problem \textperiodcentered{} 02}

\begin{problem}[Investigate, justify, conclude]
Choose 11 distinct integers from 1 to 20. Write each as $2^{k}m$ with m odd and $k \geq  0$. How many values of m are possible? Prove that one selected integer divides another. Show that the conclusion can fail with only ten integers.
\end{problem}
